system.integrity: Controlled reconstruction based on documented SEMS functional areas. Not original production SEMS source. Runtime values are measured SEMS-R traces.

runtime_interactions.note: Measured SEMS-R traces. Not production SEMS traffic. component_entity_counts are request-level co-occurrence (component on the same request as a queried table), not per-query attribution.

system.name: SEMS-R
system.description: A reconstructed university education-management system used as an experimental monolith. It is based on documented SEMS functional areas, not original production source.

known_cross_domain_dependencies: Grade workflows require student, teacher, course, and often enrollment records.
Attendance workflows require student, teacher, course, and enrollment records.
Finance workflows require student and faculty context for invoicing and ledgers.
Library membership is issued to students and staff.
Student information is read by Student, Grade, Attendance, Finance, and Library.
Course ownership sits with Faculty administration but is consumed by Student, Grade, and Attendance.

integrity.statement: These are explicit migration constraints for evidence-constrained decomposition. They do not encode a Faculty->faculty-service mapping. Algorithms must reason from evidence plus these rules.

rules.statement: Decompose the legacy system into independently deployable services.
Prefer database ownership by one service.
Prefer boundaries aligned with business capabilities.
Identify cases in which strict isolation would create excessive communication.
Explicitly report uncertain architectural decisions instead of silently guessing.
